title: Project Valhalla, Explained: How a Decade of Work Arrives in JDK 28
summary: Project Valhalla is a Java/JVM initiative that has been in development for about a decade, introducing value types (inline classes) to Java. It allows primitive-like performance with object-like behavior, solving the classic tension between primitives and objects by enabling 'value classes' that combine the best of both worlds without boxing overhead.
problem_solved: Eliminates the performance penalty and memory inefficiency of boxing primitives in collections, allowing developers to have both the speed of primitives and the flexibility of objects.
why_valuable: It brings massive performance improvements for Java applications, especially those processing large datasets, by enabling better memory layout and cache efficiency while maintaining clean object-oriented semantics.
